candidates.title: Authenticated users bypass the content_report throttle — up to ~1000 report emails/day per account to the legal mailbox
candidates.description: POST /api/content-reports/ is AllowAny and every valid create enqueues a Celery task that sends an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL. The dedicated anti-spam throttle (scope 'content_report', 5/hour per IP) is implemented as ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle). DRF's AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key() returns None whenever request.user.is_authenticated, so for any logged-in user the scoped throttle never engages — only the global 'user' throttle (1000/day) applies. An attacker with a single registered account (no subscription needed) can therefore submit ~1000 reports/day, each producing a DB row, a Celery task, and an email to the legal mailbox — 200x the intended per-IP rate, and the 'user' bucket is per-account so multiple accounts multiply it. The stated purpose of the scope (settings.py:132-134 comment: 'cada POST valido envia un mail a LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL') is defeated for the entire authenticated principal class.
candidates.root_cause: ContentReportRateThrottle subclasses AnonRateThrottle (AdminApp/domains/legal/views/viewset_base.py:14-18) instead of a rate class that keys authenticated users (e.g., UserRateThrottle with the same scope, or a combined throttle). AnonRateThrottle is anonymous-only by design in DRF.
candidates.intended_behavior: The 5/hour content_report limit should apply to every caller of the public create endpoint, authenticated or not (or an equivalent per-user cap), so report-driven email volume stays bounded.

trace.description: ContentReportBaseViewSet.throttle_classes = [ContentReportRateThrottle] — the only scoped throttle on create.
class ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle): scope='content_report'. AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None for authenticated requests -> throttle skipped entirely.
create permissions = [AllowAny] — endpoint reachable with or without a session; authenticated requests fall back to the default 'user' 1000/day throttle.
CreateContentReportQuery calls send_legal_report_email.delay(report.pk) on every create.
send_legal_report_email -> NotifyContentReportQuery -> send_mail to settings.LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL (services.py:41-48), with autoretry.
'content_report': '5/hour' — the intended bound, unreachable for authenticated users.

candidates.evidence: viewset_base.py:14-18 (AnonRateThrottle subclass), viewset_config.py:22-27 (AllowAny create), services.py:16-24 + tasks.py:67-72 (email per create), settings.py:134 (5/hour scope), settings.py:81 ('user': '1000/day' fallback). DRF semantics: AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None when request.user.is_authenticated -> allow_request returns True. Legal tests cover validation and staff-only reads but never exercise the throttle for an authenticated reporter.
candidates.conditions: Attacker holds any registered platform account (free registration; no plan required). Endpoint accepts JSON POST with valid report fields.

execution.command: POST /api/content-reports/ with a valid JSON body and a session JWT/cookie, repeated in a loop
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: requests 6..1000 within the hour return 201 (each creating a ContentReport row and enqueueing an email) instead of 429; only after 1000/day does the generic user throttle engage. Anonymous callers are correctly capped at 5/hour per IP.

candidates.remediation: Replace ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle) with a throttle that covers both principal classes — e.g., pair AnonRateThrottle(scope='content_report') with UserRateThrottle(scope='content_report') in throttle_classes, or a custom SimpleRateThrottle whose get_cache_key uses 'user_pk' if authenticated else pinned IP ident. Consider also inheriting DaventProject.throttling._ResilientThrottleMixin so a Redis outage fails open consistently with the rest of the project instead of 500ing the public endpoint.

severity.rationale: Trivial to exploit by any registered user; impact is bounded per-account (~1000 emails/day + DB rows + Celery/SMTP load on an internal mailbox) but the control explicitly built to prevent this is void for authenticated callers, and account multiplication removes the practical ceiling.

candidates.title: Chat payload leaks full staff directory (ids, names/usernames, online presence) to every paying customer despite per-message anonymity
candidates.description: The support chat deliberately anonymizes staff in messages — ChatMessageSerializer.get_sender_name returns the constant 'Soporte DAVENT' for from_staff messages and the staff-thread serializer exposes customer email only to staff. However, SupportChatViewSet.list() and heartbeat() embed staff_roster() in every customer response. staff_roster() iterates User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — i.e., ALL staff and superuser accounts, not just support agents — and returns {id (DB pk), name (get_full_name() or username — a login identifier), online} for each. Any customer with a paid plan can enumerate the complete staff account directory, their real names or usernames, primary keys, and real-time presence, contradicting the anonymity boundary the rest of the feature enforces.
candidates.root_cause: staff_roster() (services.py:134-147) scopes only by is_staff+is_active with no support-role filter, and both customer-facing responses (viewset.py:105 'staff': staff_roster(), viewset.py:198) include it unconditionally.
candidates.intended_behavior: Either the roster should be limited to agents actually handling support (or return only a display-safe label), or — if showing the team is intended — it should not expose account ids/usernames/online state of every staff principal including superusers.

trace.description: Customer heartbeat() response includes 'staff': staff_roster() on every ~45s poll.
User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — all staff incl. superusers; returns id, name (full name or username), online.
get_sender_name hardcodes 'Soporte DAVENT' for staff messages — anonymity enforced per-message but bypassed via roster.

candidates.evidence: services.py:134-147 (roster query + fields), viewset.py:91-106 and 194-199 (customer payloads), serializers.py:31-37 (sender_name anonymization). Test test_customer_payload_never_leaks_staff_identity only asserts absence of email and 'Soporte DAVENT' in messages — it does not inspect the 'staff' roster key.
candidates.conditions: Attacker holds any paid non-trial plan (chat gate). Read-only enumeration; no writes.

execution.command: GET /api/chat/ or POST /api/chat/heartbeat/ with a paid customer session
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: response.staff = [{id, name, online}, ...] enumerating every active staff/superuser account; names resolve to get_full_name() or login username.

candidates.remediation: Scope the roster to support-facing staff (e.g., a dedicated flag/group or is_staff AND a support permission), return a display label instead of username when no full name exists, and drop the numeric id if the UI does not need it. If the product intent is genuinely 'show the team', document it and exclude superusers/non-support staff.

severity.rationale: Discloses staff names/usernames/ids/presence to paying customers — aids targeted phishing/credential attacks against admin accounts, but no credentials or tenant data leak and login is separately throttled.

hardening: AdminApp/domains/chat/views/viewset.py:249 — AssistantViewSet.send reads request.data.get('body') without a serializer: a JSON body of non-string type raises AttributeError on .strip() -> unhandled 500. Validate with a CharField serializer like ChatSendSerializer.

AdminApp/domains/notifications/views/viewset.py:71-73 — read() passes request.data['id'] straight into qs.filter(pk=nid): a non-numeric id raises ValueError/TypeError -> 500. Coerce/validate to int first.

AdminApp/domains/locations/views/viewset_config.py:18-21 — city_list_queryset passes raw ?province= into filter(province_id=...): non-numeric input raises ValueError -> 500 on a public anonymous endpoint. Wrap in try/except or validate digits.

McpApp/domains/skills/views/viewset.py:91-106 — McpEndpointView assumes params is a dict; a JSON-RPC params array/string makes params.get raise AttributeError -> 500. isinstance-check params before dispatch.

AdminApp/domains/legal/views/viewset_base.py:14 — ContentReportRateThrottle does not inherit DaventProject.throttling._ResilientThrottleMixin: a Redis/cache outage makes SimpleRateThrottle raise -> 500 on the public report endpoint, inconsistent with the project's deliberate fail-open throttle design.

AdminApp/domains/chat/services/services.py:97-99 — messages_payload with after>0 returns qs.filter(id__gt=after) with no LIMIT; bounded in practice by chat_send rate and own-thread scoping, but an explicit cap would bound worst-case payload.
AdminApp/domains/chat/services/services.py:52 — get_or_create_thread can race (two concurrent first-sends) -> IntegrityError -> 500; wrap in try/except IntegrityError and re-get.

AdminApp/domains/chat/services/assistant.py:164-172 + McpApp/domains/skills/services/llm.py:122-148 — assistant send is synchronous across up to 4 providers (~30s timeout each, worst ~102s per request) on sync gunicorn workers; per-user chat_send 120/hour bounds spend but there is no global/daily LLM budget — consider a per-user daily cap or async task if abuse appears.

AdminApp/domains/chat/services/services.py:140 — staff_roster() includes every is_staff user (incl. superusers); if the roster feature is kept, restrict to support agents (see candidate chat.staff-roster-leaks-all-staff-identities).
uncovered: McpApp/fastmcp_server.py http transport (streamable-http on 127.0.0.1:8100) — correct JWT + mcp_user_access gating verified in source, but whether it is ever deployed/exposed beyond localhost is environment-dependent; parent should confirm no reverse proxy maps it publicly.

Frontend rendering of chat/assistant message bodies — backend returns plain text and no v-html/markdown sink was found for these components, but a full CLIENT-SIDE pass on chat UI components was out of this unit's backend scope.
